image_description: A top-down view of a Dungeness crab (Cancer magister) positioned on a white, slightly wrinkled fabric background. The crab features a broad, oval-shaped carapace with reddish-brown coloration and lighter mottling. It has five pairs of legs extending laterally, with the first pair modified into large claws (chelipeds). The legs appear somewhat flattened and splayed. The lighting is diffuse, casting soft shadows.

artifact_observations.reasoning: The legs, particularly the distal segments, appear overly smooth and lack the fine granular texture expected of crustacean exoskeletons. Some leg tips seem to fade or merge slightly with the background fabric.
The third and fourth walking legs on the right side appear to fuse together near the body attachment point, lacking clear separation between individual limb segments.
The left claw appears disproportionately small and flattened compared to the right claw, suggesting a minor geometric inconsistency in the generation of the chelipeds.
